Hi Daniel — great to hear and thanks for the forecast.

Short answer: yes, we can structure an annual-prepay, multi-year agreement with a phased GPU/TPM ramp and explicit fallback rules. I've sketched three landing options below (quick summary) and attached a worked example. If any of these look promising, we can produce a redline SOW for internal review.

Option A — Conservative ramp (lower up-front risk)- 2-year term, annual prepay each year- Year 1: 35% of peak GPU capacity / 40% TPM- Year 2: 100% of peak (step to full in Q3)- Term discount: 15% on unit pricing for annual prepay- Milestones: quarterly usage checkpoints; 60-day remediation/fallback if not met

Option B — Balanced ramp (favored by engineering)- 3-year term, annual prepay (front-loaded Year 1)- Year 1: 50% GPUs / 55% TPM- Year 2: 80% GPUs / 85% TPM- Year 3: 100%- Term discount: 20% year-over-year applied to committed units- Includes a one-time credit if Year 1 usage is below 70% of commit

Option C — Aggressive economics (capex-like savings)- 3-year term, annual prepay with partial up-front prepay (70% Year 1)- Year 1: 70% GPUs / 75% TPM- Year 2: 90%- Year 3: 100%- Term discount: 28% + additional volume tier credits at 90%+ utilization- Stronger rollback protections and flexible model substitutions (lower-cost quantized variants)

Key contractual notes:
- Rollback/fallback: can include a controlled step-down with a smaller credit back or conversion to hosted consumption if usage undershoots for two consecutive quarters.
- GPU types: offers for A100/H100 profiles with pricing differentials in the spreadsheet.
- Amortization: attached Redwood_Commitment_Guide.xlsx includes example cashflow scenarios and HubSpot-friendly line items.

Next step: I'll loop in Sales Ops and Finance with a proposed worksheet and get a draft SOW out by EOD Wednesday. Thoughts on which option aligns best with your CFO?

Thanks,
Sofia

Sofia — ran the numbers. My initial read: Option B gives the best balance of retention + predictable cashflow and is market-competitive. A couple thoughts: 

1) We can support a 20% base term discount for a 3-year annual prepay, but make the Year 1 price slightly higher to reflect GPU reservation risk (apply a 5% front-loaded surcharge on Year 1 reconciled against utilization credits).
2) We should add a utilization true-up at the end of each year with a 90-day reconciliation window. If utilization < 60% for any year, we convert the shortfall into hosted consumption credits rather than large refunds.
3) For rollback language: propose 6-month probationary window after a failed milestone before any capacity step-down; during this time we provide technical enablement to help reach targets.

I attached a redline pricing table in Redwood_SOW_v3.pdf and a simple amortization snapshot. If Ben can comment on legal exposure for the 6-month probation, we can finalize.

Quick legal read — ok with the proposed structure but flag two items:

1) Make the rollback path unilateral only after two consecutive quarterly misses and after the 6-month remediation window; require a 30-day notice and allow ZenithSys to convert unused committed GPU-hours into hosted consumption at a pre-agreed blended rate to avoid refunds.
2) Include a clause limiting model substitution: we can substitute to quantized variants for cost reasons, but not to different architecture classes without mutual consent.

I'll draft redline language and push to the SOW. No blockers otherwise.

Gina / Daniel — thanks, appreciate the clarity. We can do Option B with your two asks and the reconciliation automation. Summary of the agreed proposal below; I'll attach a formal SOW and amortization table by EOD Tuesday.

Agreed proposal (summary):
- Term: 3 years, annual prepay each year (invoices Year 1–3)
- Year 1 commit: 60% GPUs / 65% TPM (steeper front-load per request)
- Year 2 commit: 80% GPUs / 85% TPM
- Year 3 commit: 100%
- Pricing: base 20% term discount for the 3-year annual prepay; Year 1 surcharge +5% (reconciled as a utilization credit if annual utilization >70%)
- Utilization checkpoints: automated quarterly checks; if utilization <80% for a quarter, automatic credit issued against next invoice (credit formula included in attached amortization).
- Rollback/fallback: probationary 6-month remediation after first miss, then unilateral step-down possible after two consecutive misses with 30-day notice; unused committed credits convert to hosted consumption at blended rate.
- GPU profiles: support both A100 and H100; substitution to quantized variants allowed with prior notice unless material performance regression is observed.

Next steps: 
1) Marissa to finalize the amortization showing EBITDA and cashflow impacts with the Year 1 60% scenario (deliverable: Redwood_Amortization_ZEN_v1.xlsx).
2) Ben to provide the redline SOW clauses for rollback and substitution.
3) I'll produce the SOW (Redwood_SOW_v3.pdf) and a DocuSign route for signature.

If that all looks right, we'll target a procurement sign-off timeline of Nov 18.

Thanks and talk soon,
Sofia
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
